Sometimes I’m sure I can see clues in random patterns—license plates, warning lights in the test bay—that “prove” the world is about to end. When I’m in this amped-up state, that belief feels completely real, like there’s no point long-term because nothing will be here.

But when my energy drops for a day or two and I’m a bit calmer, that conviction loosens. I can look back and think, “That was over the top,” and the whole ‘end of the world’ thing doesn’t feel as real outside of these high, revved-up periods.

It’s been about three weeks now where I feel like I’m stuck on overdrive. I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours, but I wake up buzzing with energy, like I’ve had ten cups of coffee. I’m in the kitchen at school until they kick me out, starting new recipes, talking a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to the next. I feel incredible, like I’m meant to open the best restaurant in the city tomorrow if people would just catch up with me.

At the same time, I’ve become absolutely convinced there’s something terribly wrong inside my body. I keep thinking my organs are rotting or rearranging themselves. I’ve checked my skin in the mirror for hours, feeling like I can “sense” my liver or my heart moving around. Logically I know tests have been normal, but in these moments it feels completely real, like my body is falling apart from the inside.

What’s weird is that this intense belief and these body fears only show up when I’m in this super‑charged, sleepless state. When my mood drops back down and I’m more “normal,” those thoughts pretty much disappear.
